verses.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Cut two stone tablets like the first ones. I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
Be ready in the morning. Then come up Mount Sinai and stand in front of me there on top of the mountain.
No one is to come with you or be seen anywhere on the mountain. Not even the flocks and herds may graze in front of the mountain."
So Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones. He got up early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, carrying the two stone tablets in his hands.
Then the LORD came down in the cloud and stood there with him, and called out his name, the LORD.
The LORD passed in front of Moses, calling out, "The LORD, the LORD, the God who is merciful and kind, slow to become angry, and full of faithful love and truth.

He keeps his faithful love for thousands, and forgives wrongdoing, rebellion, and sin. But he does not let the guilty go unpunished. He punishes the children and grandchildren for the sins of their parents, to the third and fourth generation."
Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshipped.
He said, "Lord, if I have found favour with you, please go with us. Even though these people are stubborn, forgive our wrongdoing and our sin, and take us as your own people."

Then the LORD said, "Look, I am making a covenant with you. In front of all your people I will do wonders never done before in any nation in all the world. All the people around you will see the work of the LORD, because what I am going to do for you is amazing.
Obey what I command you today. Look, I will drive out ahead of you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Be careful not to make an agreement with the people who live in the land where you are going, or they will become a trap among you.
Instead, tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and cut down their Asherah poles.
Do not worship any other god, because the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

Do not make an agreement with the people who live in the land. When they chase after their gods like a prostitute and offer sacrifices to them, they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.
And you might choose some of their daughters as wives for your sons. Then those daughters would chase after their gods like prostitutes, and lead your sons to do the same.
Do not make idols out of melted metal.
Celebrate the Feast of Bread Without Yeast. For seven days eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you. Do this at the set time in the month of Abib, because in that month you came out of Egypt.
The first male born to every mother belongs to me, including all the firstborn males of your cattle and sheep.
Buy back the firstborn donkey by giving a lamb in its place. If you do not buy it back, break its neck. Buy back all your firstborn sons. No one is to come before me empty-handed.
Work for six days, but rest on the seventh day. Even during the time of ploughing and harvest you must rest.
Celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the first crops of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Gathering at the end of the year.
Three times a year all your men must come before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
I will drive out nations ahead of you and make your land larger. No one will try to take your land while you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to me together with anything made with yeast. Do not let any of the sacrifice from the Passover feast be left until morning.
Bring the best of the first crops from your land to the house of the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk."
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write down these words, because by these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.
When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the covenant in his hands, he did not know that his face was shining because he had been talking with the LORD.
When Aaron and all the people of Israel saw Moses, his face was shining, and they were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them, so Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and he spoke to them.
After that, all the people of Israel came near, and he gave them all the commands the LORD had given him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses finished speaking to them, he put a veil over his face.
But whenever he went in to speak with the LORD, he took the veil off until he came out. And when he came out and told the people of Israel what he had been commanded,
they saw that his face was shining. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in again to speak with the LORD.
